Clearing a block

Site clearing, everything above ground off the block

Clearing a block of structures, trees, stumps, vegetation and rubbish ready for construction. The scope is defined by what has to go and what has to stay, and the price is usually decided by where the material ends up rather than by how much of it there is. Tell us what is on the block, and we will quote the clearing and the disposal together.

0456 220 552

Carried out under demolition licence AD214737

Before anything starts

Six things have to be settled first, and not all of them are ours

Most jobs that run late run late on this list rather than on the work itself. Each line says who owns it.

  1. 01

    Tree approval or exemption

    Who You or your certifier

    Mature trees commonly carry a protection order or an approval condition. This is the item that most often holds a clearing job up.

  2. 02

    What stays

    Who Agreed between you and us

    Boundary fences, retained trees, a shed, a slab. Marked on site before anything starts.

  3. 03

    Service location

    Who Max, with a locator

    Stumps and old footings sit near services more often than people expect.

  4. 04

    Suspect material identified

    Who Max, through an accredited laboratory

    Old sheds, fencing and buried debris are all places fibro turns up on an older block.

  5. 05

    Access and truck standing

    Who Both of us

    Whether a truck and dog can turn decides the number of loads.

  6. 06

    Sediment control

    Who Max

    A cleared block runs water. Controlling it is a condition on most approvals.

Scope

What the quote does and does not cover

Stated side by side so there is nothing to discover later. Anything in the right hand column can be added, it is simply priced separately.

The detail

What makes a clearing job bigger than it looks

  • The trees. A mature tree can be a protected item, a crane job, or both. It is the single most common reason a clearing quote and a clearing job differ.
  • The destination of the material. Green waste, clean concrete, mixed rubbish and anything contaminated go to four different places at four different rates.
  • What is buried. Old slabs, footings, fill and occasionally buried building waste. None of it is visible from the street.
  • What has to stay. A retained tree or a shared fence turns open clearing into careful work around a thing that must not be damaged.
  • Access. Whether a truck and dog can get in and turn changes the number of loads for the same volume of material.
  • Whether fibro is present. On an older block, old sheds and fencing are both likely candidates and both have to be dealt with under the asbestos pathway.

What we need to quote it

The address
So we can look at access and what is around it
Photographs
One from the street and one of the work itself
Any reports you hold
Hazardous materials, structural, survey or levels
Your dates
What has to be finished by when, and what is waiting on it

We attend the site before quoting anything substantial.

Old sheds and fencing are where fibro hides

On a block built before 1990, the shed, the fence and the garage are as likely to be asbestos as the house is. It is identified and removed under clearance before the clearing starts.

Before you book

What people ask about this one

Do you remove trees?
Yes, as part of clearing, where approval permits it. Getting that approval is yours or your certifier’s job, and it is worth starting early because it is usually the long pole.
What about the stumps?
Ground out or grubbed out, depending on what is going on top of them afterwards. A stump left under a future slab is a problem for somebody later.
Is clearing the same as demolition?
They overlap and often run together, but they are different scopes. Demolition is the structure. Clearing is everything else on the block.
What if we find buried rubbish?
It is assessed and, if it is suspect, sampled before it moves. Buried building waste on an older block is common enough that it is worth allowing for.
What condition is the block left in?
Cleared and graded, with the material gone and the dockets handed over. Levelling to a design platform is excavation work and is a separate scope.

Get a quote

Send photographs from the street and the rear

Two photographs and a note about what has to stay is most of a clearing scope. If there are mature trees, say so, because that is the item that moves the dates.

  • Material separated on the way out so it leaves on the right rate
  • Suspect material identified before anything is disturbed
  • Cartage on the same contract
